scope: Combined eight-cycle preflight of6324 with real weather/uploads, four AP outages, supervisor and independent UART guard. Not a24-hour or steady-state memory acceptance.

workload.scope:
Observe native Small TV heap/stack during real HTTP/weather/photo activity.

The requested cycle count or guest duration defines this workload's scope.
Short runs do not establish the 24-hour H10 or physical-board acceptance.
The guest runs its unmodified archived application. Hardware breakpoints and
read-only RSP inspect SDK counters; no guest functions are called by the host.
limitations: Native firmware only; no factory heap/stack equivalence claim.
Short workload is not the 24-hour H10 or physical-board acceptance.
Stack fill is a historical SDK watermark; sampled frames do not prove all execution peaks.
Sum of per-heap minimum counters follows SDK semantics, not a simultaneous global minimum.

rom_counter_crosscheck.scope: Exact two ROM getters executed outside the VM on copied typed headers, not invoked in the guest.

supervisor.scope: Child process supervision only; not a 24-hour or memory-trend acceptance.

analysis.scope:
Audit a native runtime journal and compare free heap in equal workload phases.

This reads files only and never connects to or pauses the guest. A diagnostic
prefix of an active workload is explicitly pending, never a completed H10 pass.

limitations: Observed phase/window medians and variation do not prove absence of every possible leak.
SDK minimum is cumulative; a constant minimum can coexist with declining current free heap.
Retained changes require an explanation or a firmware fix before accepting the soak.
This audits native QEMU runtime only; it does not establish physical-board acceptance.
The workload uses a fixed NTP epoch; this is not a continuous calendar/DST test.
Task stack fill and sampled free heap cannot prove every interrupt or transient allocation peak.
Retained memory loss is a finding to investigate, not automatically an allowed SDK cache.
